title: Model Factory catalog
description: Every Model Factory step and format, deduplicated across the quantise, build, evaluate and deploy research areas and the end-to-end CPU feasibility run. Each step says whether it was run in the research sandbox (verified_here) and what was not verified. Companion to MODEL_FACTORY.md.

hardware_targets.owner_box: 2x RTX 3090 24 GB (48 GB, NVLink, sm_86), i9-12900KS, 64 GB RAM, Ubuntu; TabbyAPI (EXL2/EXL3, ~100 tok/s), Strata (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GGUF with experts in VRAM), llama.cpp, gpt-oss-120b; 262,144-token contexts; reached over Tailscale only
hardware_targets.research_sandbox: Ubuntu 24.04, 4 shared vCPUs (load average 3-5 from sibling agents), ~15 GB RAM, 1.6-5 GB free disk, no GPU (nvidia-smi rc=9), egress via proxy (GitHub and PyPI worked)

variables.MF: Model Factory tool home on the machine, e.g. /opt/seraphina/model-factory (venvs/, llama.cpp/, exllamav3/, tabbyAPI/, recipes/, locks/, help/)
variables.MFS: the factory's gate and step scripts (prototypes listed under 'prototypes'; to be ported into the Harness)
variables.REG: registry root on the large models filesystem, e.g. /srv/models (never the root filesystem)
variables.NAME: registry model name, e.g. qwen3-8b
variables.OUT: the variant being made (in $WORK until the gates pass, then moved to $REG/models/$NAME/<format>/<quant>)

conventions.python: Gate scripts run with python3 -I (isolated) and get every path as an argument; never run an interpreter from inside a downloaded model folder. The llama.cpp converters are the exception: they import their own sibling package, so they run without -I from the pinned checkout.

exit_codes.gates: 0 pass, 1 fail, 2 unparseable/missing input (re-run up to 2 times)
exit_codes.fetch_pinned: 0 ok, 1 licence not allowed, 2 network, 3 gated (needs-human), 4 not found/private, 5 disk
exit_codes.mf_deploy: 0 deployed, 1 refused before any change, 2 failed and restored, 3 restore failed (needs-human)
exit_codes.mf_broker: 0 granted/released, 10 blocked by window, 11 GPU busy, 12 not enough VRAM or GPU state unknown (services restored), 13 a service did not come back healthy (needs-human)

steps.title: Build llama.cpp at a pinned commit (CPU here; CUDA sm_86 on the owner's box)
steps.plain: Downloads and compiles llama.cpp, the toolkit that converts, quantises, measures and serves GGUF models. The exact git commit is recorded, because a shallow clone always reports 'build 1', so the build number means nothing.
steps.tool_version: llama.cpp 8baabd5 (tag b11785, 2026-10-21, ggml 0.27.0, prints 0.7.0-dev) for the quantise, evaluate and deploy research; eb182d8 (same day, 0.7.0-dev) for the end-to-end feasibility run
commands: git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp.git $MF/llama.cpp && git -C $MF/llama.cpp rev-parse HEAD
# pin an exact commit later: git -C $MF/llama.cpp fetch --depth 1 origin <sha> && git -C $MF/llama.cpp checkout <sha>

cmake --build $MF/llama.cpp/build -j4 --target llama-quantize llama-imatrix llama-perplexity llama-gguf-split llama-server llama-bench llama-batched-bench llama-fit-params llama-cli llama-gguf-hash ggml-rpc-server   # verified; the RPC target is ggml-rpc-server, not rpc-server

cmake -S $MF/llama.cpp -B $MF/llama.cpp/build-cuda -DGGML_CUDA=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=86 -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release && cmake --build $MF/llama.cpp/build-cuda -j --target llama-quantize llama-imatrix llama-perplexity llama-gguf-split llama-server llama-bench llama-batched-bench llama-fit-params llama-cli   # RTX 3090 = sm_86; NOT verified (no CUDA here)
for t in llama-quantize llama-imatrix llama-perplexity llama-server llama-bench llama-fit-params llama-gguf-split; do $LCPP/$t --help > $MF/help/$t.txt 2>&1; done
outputs: $LCPP/{llama-quantize, llama-imatrix, llama-perplexity, llama-gguf-split, llama-server, llama-bench, llama-batched-bench, llama-fit-params, llama-cli, llama-gguf-hash, ggml-rpc-server}
$MF/VERSIONS.txt with the git commit
$MF/help/*.txt (captured --help)
steps.resources: Measured on 4 shared vCPUs: 7 min 15 s for 7 targets (feasibility run), about 10-15 min for the full target list; about 5 GB RAM during the build; build directory about 80 MB with only these targets; source tree 220-250 MB. On an i9-12900KS roughly 2-3 min for CPU and 5-20 min for CUDA (estimates). Independent of model size.
checks: llama-cli --version contains the pinned commit (never the build number)
every target exists and '<tool> --help' exits 0
llama-quantize --help lists Q4_K_M, IQ4_XS, MXFP4_MOE and Q1_0
llama-bench JSON field build_commit equals the pinned commit (cross-check)
pitfalls: The llama-server web UI is fetched at build time from huggingface.co. Offline, the build still succeeds but logs 'UI: embedded 0 assets'; the API works but a novice gets no web page. Supply a pre-downloaded tools/ui/dist or fail the 'novice web UI' check.

Defaults in this build differ from older guides: llama-server port 9931 (not 8080), --fit on, -ngl auto, -np auto (4 unified slots), --jinja on, --cache-ram 8192 MiB, and --no-mmap/--mlock replaced by --load-mode none|mmap|mlock|mmap+mlock|dio.
A shallow clone reports build_number=1 in llama-bench and the server, so record the git sha.
steps.verification: CPU build verified three times (8baabd5 twice, eb182d8 once). The CUDA build and every -ngl/-fa/-sm behaviour are not verified.

Never install llmcompressor into the vLLM venv.
Without protobuf, transformers 5 cannot convert a SentencePiece tokenizer.model and fails with a misleading '`tiktoken` is required' error.
huggingface_hub 2.2.0 ships only the `hf` CLI; there is no `huggingface-cli`, although the mergekit README still says to run it.
Licence: the Unsloth wheel metadata says Apache-2.0, but unsloth_cli/* and studio/* carry 'SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only'. Bundling Unsloth Studio inside the Harness has AGPL consequences.
Thread oversubscription: on a busy 4-vCPU box a torch training step took about 10 s with 4 threads versus 0.5 s with 1. The broker sets OMP_NUM_THREADS and llama.cpp -t per job.
GPTQModel's default offload_to_disk_path is under /tmp; point it at the models filesystem.
In the evaluation sandbox the lmeval venv borrowed torch/datasets/transformers from another venv through a .pth file to save 5.7 GB; on the owner's box install it normally.

steps.title: ExLlamaV3, ExLlamaV2 (legacy) and TabbyAPI at pinned commits (CUDA only)
steps.plain: Fetches the EXL3 quantiser and the TabbyAPI server the owner uses for the fastest GPU-only serving, plus the old EXL2 tools for rebuilding legacy quants. These need an NVIDIA GPU and CUDA, so here they were only read, not run.
steps.tool_version: exllamav3 v1.6.4 (da68d57, 2026-10-21); exllamav2 0.3.2 (repo 7dc12af, 2026-03-04); TabbyAPI main a270c55 (2026-10-19, pins exllamav3 v1.6.3, no release numbers). TabbyAPI removed the ExLlamaV2 backend in c8b9a8f (2026-07-14); the last commit with it is 79126f904c2e00aece026b36bb70bbb87e4892b2.
commands: git clone --depth 1 --branch v1.6.4 https://github.com/turboderp-org/exllamav3.git $MF/exllamav3 && cd $MF/exllamav3 && uv venv && uv sync --extra cu128   # CUDA only; NOT verified
# alternative: a release wheel named like exllamav3-<ver>+cu128.torch2.9.0-cp313-cp313-linux_x86_64.whl (the pattern TabbyAPI pins for 1.6.3)
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/turboderp-org/exllamav2.git $MF/exllamav2   # legacy EXL2 only, CUDA only
git clone https://github.com/theroyallab/tabbyAPI $MF/tabbyAPI && git -C $MF/tabbyAPI checkout a270c55
git clone https://github.com/theroyallab/tabbyAPI $MF/tabbyAPI-exl2 && git -C $MF/tabbyAPI-exl2 checkout 79126f904c2e00aece026b36bb70bbb87e4892b2   # only while EXL2 models are still served
cd $MF/tabbyAPI && ./venv/bin/python main.py --help   # 653-line help; every config key is also a --kebab-case flag (verified, started without exllamav3 via developer.unsafe_launch)

outputs: $MF/exllamav3 (convert.py, eval/*.py, util/*.py, sc_*.py)
$MF/exllamav2
$MF/tabbyAPI (+ optional pinned $MF/tabbyAPI-exl2)
steps.resources: Small checkouts. The CUDA extension is JIT-compiled at first import (minutes on the GPU box, estimate).
checks: git rev-parse HEAD equals the pinned commit for each checkout
exllamav3 __version__ == '1.6.4'; TabbyAPI's pyproject exllamav3 pin recorded in the Blueprint
'python convert.py -h' succeeds on the GPU box (here it fails with 'OSError: CUDA_HOME not set' while JIT-building the extension)
the exllamav3 version that makes a quant is not newer than the one the serving TabbyAPI loads, unless a load test passed

steps.title: Detect the hardware the model has to fit on
steps.plain: Reads how many GPUs there are, how much free memory each has, whether they are joined by NVLink, and how much system RAM and disk are free. Every 'will it fit' answer starts from these numbers.
steps.tool_version: llama.cpp b11785; NVIDIA driver as installed on the owner's box
commands: nvidia-smi topo -m        # 'NV#' between GPU0 and GPU1 means NVLink
$LCPP/llama-server --list-devices   # verified with two RPC devices: 'RPC0: 127.0.0.1:50152 (16093 MiB, 16093 MiB free)'
grep -E 'MemTotal|MemAvailable' /proc/meminfo; nproc; lscpu | grep -E 'Model name|Thread|Core'; df -B1 --output=avail $REG
outputs: hardware.json {gpus:[{index, name, total_mib, free_mib, pcie_gen, pcie_width}], nvlink, ram_avail_mib, cpu_threads, disk_free_bytes, measured_with:[services holding VRAM]}
steps.resources: Seconds; no GPU work.
checks: number of nvidia-smi rows == number of CUDA devices in --list-devices
every GPU has free_mib > 0, recorded together with the services that held VRAM at that moment
NVLink flag recorded (it selects TabbyAPI tensor_parallel_backend nccl vs native)
ram_avail_mib > 0 and disk_free_bytes recorded for the registry filesystem
pitfalls: Free VRAM is a moment in time. Measure with the serving models stopped, or record which services held memory, otherwise the fit verdict is wrong.
llama.cpp splits layers by FREE memory by default, so a GPU partly used by another server gets fewer layers unless -ts is given.
Unsloth's NVLINK_P2P.md: on PCIe P2P under IOMMU, peer copies can be silently dropped and look like a 'broken quant'. Only rely on P2P when topo shows NV#.
In this sandbox nvidia-smi exists but fails with rc=9 ('couldn't communicate with the NVIDIA driver'): a real 'GPU state unknown' case that must fail closed.
steps.verification: --list-devices verified with two RPC devices standing in for GPUs; nvidia-smi output on a real driver not verified.

steps.title: Inventory and gate the owner's existing quants
steps.plain: Before making anything new, scans the folders of models the owner has already quantised and works out each one's format, checks every file is intact, records its sha256 and how it was made, and flags files the current servers can no longer load or that have no surviving full-precision source.
steps.tool: gguf_gate.py, hf_quant_gate.py (stdlib + gguf-py; headers only, never loads weights)
commands: for f in $(find $MODELS -name '*.gguf' | grep -v -E -- '-000(0[2-9]|[1-9][0-9])-of-'); do $MF/venvs/convert/bin/python -I $MFS/gguf_gate.py "$f" --sha256 --json "$INV/$(basename "$f").json"; done
for d in $(find $MODELS -name config.json -printf '%h\n' | sort -u); do python3 -I $MFS/hf_quant_gate.py "$d" --sha256 --json "$INV/$(basename "$d").json"; done
inputs: $MODELS: the owner's model folders (GGUF files, EXL2/EXL3/GPTQ/AWQ/compressed-tensors folders)
outputs: $INV/*.json per artifact: format, architecture, file_type/quant_method, bpw, tensor/type counts, imatrix provenance (quantize.imatrix.file/dataset/chunks_count), EXL3 version/bits/head_bits/calibration rows x cols, sha256 per file
an inventory card per model: loadable by which engine, BF16 source found or missing
steps.resources: Header reads take seconds per model. sha256 is disk-bound, about 1-2 GB/s on NVMe (a 70 GB folder takes about 1 min). Almost no RAM; no GPU.
checks: gguf_gate exit 2 = truncated, unreadable or missing shard (verified by deleting shard 2 of 3) -> quarantine
file_type not in {ALL_F32, MOSTLY_F16, MOSTLY_BF16} -> 'quantized'; never a source for further quantisation
empty imatrix keys on an IQ1/IQ2/IQ3_XXS/Q2_K_S file -> flag (llama.cpp would have refused, so the file came from elsewhere)

steps.title: Will it fit? Analytic estimate before and after download
steps.plain: Predicts the GPU memory and RAM a model needs at a given context length and KV-cache type, and where each layer goes on two GPUs. For MoE models it finds the smallest number of expert layers to keep in RAM and prints the exact llama.cpp flags. Before download it works from config.json and a target bits-per-weight; after conversion from the exact GGUF tensor sizes.
steps.tool_version: fit_calc.py prototype with placement rules copied from llama.cpp b11785 src/llama-model.cpp:1638-1695, src/llama-context.cpp:377-383 and 515-545, src/llama-kv-cache-iswa.cpp:73, src/llama-hparams.cpp:208-258; exllamav3 1.6.4
commands: $LCPP/llama-quantize --dry-run $REG/models/$NAME/gguf/BF16/$NAME-BF16.gguf Q4_K_M   # prints 'quant size = X MiB (Y BPW)' and per-tensor targets, writes nothing (verified)
cd $MF/exllamav3 && python util/size_estimation.py -i $OUT/exl3-4.0bpw [-or override.yaml]   # unverified (CUDA import)
inputs: target contexts, cache types, slots (-np), ubatch, split mode, concurrency
outputs: fit.json: per context per-GPU weights/KV/compute MiB, host MiB, fits, n_cpu_moe, ts, suggested_llama_flags; max_ctx_fitting; layer_kinds
plan.json candidates [{format, type/bpw, est_weight_bytes, est_kv_bytes, placement (all-GPU | experts-on-CPU), server}]
steps.resources: Milliseconds to 2 s (reads only the GGUF header and tensor index); a dry run needs the BF16 GGUF to exist (mmap'd, not quantised). No GPU.
checks: exit 0 = every requested context fits; exit 1 = at least one does not (results[].fits false)

weights_mib and kv_mib agree with 'llama-fit-params --fit-print on' within max(2 MiB, 5%) (verified on tiny-llama and tiny-mixtral over 2 RPC devices for -ngl 99, -ts 3,1, -ngl 2, q8_0 KV, -ncmoe 0/1/2)
KV check against llama.cpp's own CUDA sample: Qwen3-30B-A3B (48 layers, 4 KV heads, head_dim 128, f16) at 4096 ctx = 48*2*4*128*2*4096 = 384 MiB, the reported 'context 384'
compute_mib_heuristic >= the measured compute buffer (Qwen3-30B-A3B sample: about 930 vs 898)
all-GPU candidate passes only if weights + KV + compute + 1024 MiB margin <= free VRAM on every GPU
hybrid MoE candidate: non-expert weights + KV <= VRAM and CPU-resident expert bytes + --cache-ram + 8 GiB OS headroom <= RAM
reject IQ1_*/IQ2_XXS/IQ2_XS/IQ2_S/IQ3_XXS/Q2_K_S candidates with no imatrix planned (llama.cpp hard-fails; verified)
warn when ctx > n_ctx_train (llama-server caps the slot context and logs 'capping')
pitfalls: At 262K context the KV cache can exceed the weights: a dense 64-layer model with 8 KV heads of 128 needs 64 GiB in f16 and about 34 GiB in q8_0. Plan KV quantisation (llama.cpp -ctk/-ctv q8_0; TabbyAPI cache_mode 'k,v' bits 2-8) together with the weight quant.
The compute buffer is a heuristic and the CUDA context (about 0.3-0.6 GiB per GPU) is not in it; keep --margin 1024 (the same default as --fit-target).

llama.cpp turns on pipeline parallelism (4 compute-buffer copies) only when there is more than one device, every layer and the output are offloaded, split is 'layer', KV is offloaded and no tensor overrides are set. Any -ot or --n-cpu-moe turns it off (verified: compute on RPC0 fell from 28 to 8 MiB with -ncmoe 1).
--n-cpu-moe offloads the experts of the FIRST N layers; with the default -ts GPU0 ends nearly empty, so the calculator re-packs and emits '-ts a,b'.

SWA patterns are hard-coded per architecture in llama.cpp, not in the GGUF (gpt-oss 2, gemma3 6, cohere2 4, llama4 4 chunked 8192, exaone4 4); an unknown architecture falls back to all-full-attention, an upper bound.
MLA (DeepSeek/Kimi) KV is approximated as kv_lora_rank + 64 per token; not verified against a real file.
BF16 of a 70B dense model (140 GB) exceeds 48 GB VRAM + 64 GB RAM: imatrix and KLD for such models run from a Q8_0 GGUF.
The HF-config mode uses one bpw for every layer; real GGUF mixes shift sizes by several percent. Re-run with --gguf once the file exists.
steps.verification: Calculator verified against llama-fit-params on two tiny models over two RPC devices; the dry run verified. EXL3 size estimation not run.

outputs: fit-print.txt: one line per device 'NAME model_MiB context_MiB compute_MiB'
fitted-args.txt: '-c N -ngl N [-ts ...] [-ot "..."]'

checks: every fit-print line parses as '<dev> <int> <int> <int>'
for each GPU: model + context + compute <= free_mib - margin
the fitted -c >= the requested context (--fit silently lowers -c down to --fit-ctx, default 4096)
plan.fit-estimate agrees within tolerance, otherwise flag 'calculator drift' for that architecture

steps.title: Book the GPUs, RAM and disk through the resource broker
steps.plain: Quantising, fine-tuning, measuring and loading models all need the GPUs. The broker is the only thing that hands them out: it refuses inside someone else's reserved window, refuses if another job holds the GPU, never stops a serving model without approval, checks there is enough free VRAM, RAM and disk, and gives the job a lease with an expiry.
steps.tool: mf_broker.py (flock-serialised JSON state; nvidia-smi for VRAM); systemd-inhibit
commands: # services.json entry: "tabby": {"gpus":[0,1], "owner":"serving", "stop_cmd":"systemctl --user stop mf-tabbyapi", "start_cmd":"systemctl --user start mf-tabbyapi", "is_running_cmd":"systemctl --user is-active --quiet mf-tabbyapi", "health_url":"http://127.0.0.1:5000/health"}

systemd-inhibit --what=shutdown:sleep --who=seraphina-model-factory --why="quantising <name> to EXL3" --mode=block <job command>   # stops reboots by tools that respect logind (design; from the restore research)
inputs: job id, owner, gpus, minutes, vram_gib (+ ram_gib, disk_gib, cpu_threads in the design)
approval token when a serving service must stop
outputs: state.json lease {owner, gpus, started, expires, stopped_services, free_vram_gib}
exit 0 granted / 10 blocked by window / 11 GPU busy / 12 not enough VRAM or GPU state unknown (services restored)
steps.resources: Negligible. Stopping a serving model costs its reload later (about 10 s to several minutes for 40-60 GB from NVMe).
checks: a window held by another owner overlapping [now, now+minutes] on any requested GPU -> exit 10, nothing stopped (verified)
an active lease on any requested GPU -> exit 11 (verified)

design rule (not in the prototype): stopping any service whose owner is 'serving' needs an approval: a standing approval on the current maintenance window for that service, or a one-click approval; otherwise the job waits in the queue as needs-human
after grant: each stopped service's is_running_cmd fails; services on other GPUs still answer /health 200 (verified: the GPU0 server kept serving while GPU1 was leased)
free VRAM summed over leased GPUs >= vram_gib, else services restored and exit 12 (verified with a fixture nvidia-smi)
nvidia-smi failing (rc=9 here) with vram_gib set -> exit 12 gpu_state_unknown, services restored (verified)
disk: free >= planned bytes x 1.1 + 1 GiB on the registry filesystem (design)
pitfalls: VRAM frees asynchronously after a stop; poll nvidia-smi until used memory stops falling (or compute-apps is empty) before measuring. The prototype measures once.
Any exception after stopping services must restart them. A first prototype crashed and left a server down; the current one restores in try/except (keep as a test case).
Never stop a service that serves someone else's window even if the GPUs look idle; the window check comes before any stop.
One broker per machine: every factory (software jobs that call local models, model jobs, fine-tunes, system maintenance) must go through it, or leases mean nothing.
steps.verification: Windows, busy GPU, VRAM shortfall, unknown GPU state, healthy restore and reaping verified with sandbox services and a fixture nvidia-smi. The approval rule is design only.

steps.title: Give the GPUs back and confirm every stopped server is healthy
steps.plain: When a job ends (or its lease runs out), the broker restarts every server it stopped for that job, unless another job still holds the GPU, and waits for each to report healthy. A server that does not come back becomes a needs-human card instead of being silently left down.
commands: python3 -I $MFS/mf_broker.py --dir $REG/broker reap   # systemd timer every 5 min: release expired leases
outputs: lease removed from state.json; per service: healthy | UNHEALTHY | left stopped (GPU still leased)
exit 0 / 13 (a service did not come back: needs-human)
steps.resources: One restart per stopped service.
checks: exit 0 and every listed service 'healthy' (verified); exit 13 if any is UNHEALTHY
state.json no longer lists the job; no lease is past its expiry after a reap run (verified with a 0.02-minute lease)
the restart uses the deployment's current serve.env, so a release after a deploy brings back the NEW model, not a cached command line
pitfalls: Leases need an expiry; a crashed job without one would hold a GPU forever.
If the deploy changed what a service runs, restart it from the deployment's serve.env.
steps.verification: Healthy restart and reaping verified in the sandbox.

steps.tool: fetch_pinned.py (huggingface_hub snapshot_download), or hf download + hf cache verify
commands: hf download <repo> --revision <sha> --dry-run --format json   # size plan without downloading
outputs: $REG/models/<name>/hf/bf16/ (Hub snapshot)
source.json (repo_id, requested_revision, commit, licence, gated, params, per-file algo/hash/size, fetched_utc)
steps.resources: Disk about 2 bytes/param for BF16 (8B ~16 GB, 32B ~64 GB, 70B ~141 GB) plus 5% + 1 GiB headroom. Streaming, small RAM. Hashing is one full read (about 1-2 min per 16 GB on NVMe, estimate). No GPU.

LFS files: sha256 == Hub lfs.sha256; non-LFS files: git-blob-sha1 == Hub blob_id (sha1('blob <size>\0'+bytes), verified equal to `git hash-object`)
each file's size == Hub size; no missing files
--verify-only exit 0 (a 1-byte corruption in a shard gives exit 1 naming that shard; verified)
no .bin/.pt/.pth/.ckpt downloaded unless --allow-pickle was approved

`hf download --local-dir` creates DIR/.cache/huggingface/download/*.metadata, and `hf cache verify --local-dir --fail-on-extra-files` reports them as extra (reproduced). Delete .cache first or do not use that flag.
Meta repos ship duplicate pickle weights under original/; exclude them.
Only the verifier ran (offline, against a synthetic source.json); download itself was blocked here.

steps.title: Inspect the HF-format folder before any GPU time (shards, index, config, tokenizer, eos, context)

agent models: tool_schema_rendered, tool_call_rendered and tool_result_rendered all true (--require-tools)

steps.title: GGUF quality: KL-divergence, same-top-token agreement and perplexity against the base
steps.plain: Records the original model's full next-token probabilities once, then measures how far each quant drifts from them token by token, on a fixed test text. Mean KLD and 'same top token %' are the quality gate; perplexity is only a secondary check. A novice can read the result as 'agrees with the original 96% of the time'.
commands: $LCPP/llama-perplexity -m $BF16 -f $EVAL -c 512 -b 512 --chunks 100 -ngl 999 -fa on --fit off -t 8 --kl-divergence-base $WORK/$NAME-base.kld > $WORK/ppl-base.log 2>&1   # base pass: plain PPL + saved reference logits (verified on CPU without -ngl/-fa)

$LCPP/llama-perplexity -m $OUT/$NAME-Q4_K_M.gguf --kl-divergence-base $WORK/$NAME-base.kld --kl-divergence -c 512 -b 512 -ngl 999 -fa on --fit off -t 8 > $WORK/kld-Q4_K_M.log 2>&1   # tokens come from the .kld file; -c must equal the base run; never pass --chunks
$LCPP/llama-perplexity -m $BF16 --kl-divergence-base $WORK/$NAME-base.kld --kl-divergence -c 512 -b 512 -t 8   # sanity: base against itself must give KLD 0 (verified: 0.000000, same-top 99.98%)

python3 -I $MFS/ppl_kld_gate.py --kld-log $WORK/kld-Q4_K_M.log --max-mean-kld 0.05 --max-p99-kld 0.6 --min-same-top 92 --max-ppl-ratio 1.04 --json $WORK/q4km.gate.json   # prototype A: exit 0 pass / 1 fail / 2 unparseable (verified)
# KV-cache cost on the same weights (verified): add -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -fa on (or q4_0) to the --kl-divergence run; gate the KV type the server will actually run
inputs: BF16 reference GGUF (or Q8_0 when BF16 does not fit; recorded as the reference)
$EVAL (same file, ctx and chunk count for every candidate)
outputs: $WORK/$NAME-base.kld (reference logits; deleted after the ladder)
per-quant logs
gate JSON {ppl_q, ppl_base, ppl_ratio, mean_kld, median_kld, p99_kld, p999_kld, max_kld, same_top_p_pct, rms_dp_pct, cor_ln_ppl_pct}
steps.resources: Base logit file = 20 + chunks x n_ctx x 4 + chunks x (n_ctx/2 - 1) x (2 x ceil_even(n_vocab) + 8) bytes (verified exactly: 67,108,372 B for 64 x 512 with vocab 2048; 62.9 MB for 60 x 512 in the feasibility run). With a 151,936 vocab at 100 x 512 that is about 7.7 GB; the whole wikitext-2 (~570 chunks) about 44 GB. Compute: one forward pass of chunks x n_ctx tokens per quant (GPU minutes). Tiny models on CPU: 3-7.5 s per pass.
checks: log contains '====== KL divergence statistics ======' and 'Same top p:'; otherwise exit 2 and re-run up to 2 times
base log contains 'Final estimate: PPL = X +/- Y'; use it as ppl_base (the KLD-mode 'Mean PPL(base)' came out 0.58% low: 312.56 vs 314.37)
ppl_q from the KLD-mode run equals a plain run (verified), so one run per quant is enough
mean KLD, p99 KLD and same-top within the policy class for the quant's bits (policy.quality)
PPL ratio only as a secondary check (policy.quality.max_ppl_ratio; report-only at 3 bits and below)

ladder sanity within one family (K or IQ): a higher-bpw quant must not have a mean KLD more than 10% above a lower-bpw one (verified ladder on tiny-llama: Q8_0 8.51 bpw KLD 0.00002 / 99.39%; Q4_K_M 5.00 bpw 0.00128 / 96.11%; Q2_K 3.36 bpw 0.02039 / 87.73%; IQ2_XXS 2.60 bpw 0.03197 / 86.03%)
self-KLD of the base == 0 (wrong-reference detector)
KV-cache gate on the served cache type (verified: q8_0 KV on Q8_0 weights KLD 0.000034; q4_0 KV 0.00155 / 95.97%, about the damage of Q4_K_M weights)
corpus sha256, ctx and chunks identical between base and candidate
pitfalls: llama-perplexity can exit 0 after a failure or without the final statistics (1 of 3 identical runs here; also 'failed to decode'). Gate on the parsed block, never on the exit code.
In --kl-divergence mode a different -c gave 'failed to find a memory slot ... failed to decode' and --chunks 32 processed 64 chunks with no summary; both exited 0.

Perplexity alone misleads: IQ2_XXS had PPL ratio 1.001 (another run 0.956, better than base) but the worst KLD and 83.6% top-1; Q8_0 had a lower PPL than f16 (102.30 vs 102.31, inside the ±1.76 error bar).
Only the second half of each chunk is scored, so different -c values are not comparable; never compare across tokenizers or families.
Check disk before creating the base logit file and delete it afterwards.
A bf16 base that does not fit 48 GB VRAM runs with partial offload (slow, once per model) or Q8_0 is used as the reference; record which.
The tiny-model absolute KLD values (Q4_K_M 0.001-0.0017) do not transfer to real models; the thresholds must be calibrated per family against its own Q8_0.
steps.verification: Base and candidate passes, gates, ladder, KV-cache cost and self-KLD verified on three tiny models on CPU.

steps.title: EXL3 perplexity, KL-divergence and KV-cache sweep (exllamav3)
steps.plain: The same quality checks for EXL3 models served by TabbyAPI. The '-g' mode reproduces llama.cpp's perplexity method, so EXL3 and GGUF quants of one model can be ranked on one scale; model_diff gives KLD and top-K agreement against the original.
commands: cd $MF/exllamav3 && python eval/ppl.py -m $OUT/exl3-4.00bpw -g -c 512   # GGUF-equivalent wikitext-2 PPL
python eval/model_diff.py -ma $SRC -mb $OUT/exl3-4.00bpw -r 100 -l 2048 -d 0   # KL-div A||B and B||A, top-K agreement
python eval/model_diff.py -ma $OUT/exl3-4.00bpw -mb $OUT/exl3-4.00bpw -cqs   # KLD for every k,v cache-bit pair: choose TabbyAPI cache_mode
python eval/qbench.py $WORK/project.yaml -d 0   # reference engine transformers; candidates exllamav3 or llamacpp (llama-cpp-python); qb_results.json + KLD/VRAM plots
# common model flags (exllamav3/model_init.py): -gs 22,24 (GB per GPU), -tp, -tpb nccl, -mcl N (experts of first N MoE layers on CPU), -cs cache tokens, -cq 8,8
inputs: HF reference (bf16) or a higher-bpw EXL3
outputs: exl3-ppl.log ('Final estimate: PPL = X +/- Y' in -g mode; ' -- Perplexity: X' in native mode)
model_diff.log (' -- KL divergence (A, B): x', ' -- Top-K agreement, A vs B:' with 'K = 1: 0.xxxx')
qb_results.json
steps.resources: GPU-bound, similar to the llama.cpp passes. model_diff holds both models' active layers (-kb keeps only some modules of B resident). The HF reference can stream layer by layer (options.streaming: true) with a logit cache capped by max_size_gb.
checks: -g mode: parse 'Final estimate: PPL = ' with the same regex as GGUF; compare with the GGUF quants on the same corpus
'KL divergence (A, B)' within the policy class; 'K = 1' agreement >= the class minimum; ' -- Bitrate: x bpw / y bpw (head)' == requested bits
cache sweep: choose the smallest k,v pair whose KLD is within the near-lossless class and write it to TabbyAPI cache_mode
qbench JSON contains every planned candidate and none are NaN
pitfalls: CUDA only; flags from argparse at da68d57.
ppl.py fetches wikitext from huggingface.co on first use and caches it under $TMPDIR/llama_cpp_ppl_wikitext2; pre-seed this cache offline.
qbench's llamacpp engine uses llama-cpp-python (0.3.36 on PyPI), which embeds its own llama.cpp and can lag behind new GGUF types; check it loads the file first.
steps.verification: Not run (CUDA only).

steps.title: Backend-neutral KLD for HF-format quants (transformers)
steps.plain: Measures, through one common runtime, how far each safetensors quant (GPTQ, AWQ, FP8, FP4, NF4) drifts from the original, so quants from different tools are compared on equal terms.
commands: OMP_NUM_THREADS=8 $MF/venvs/quant/bin/python -I $MFS/hf_kld.py $SRC $OUT/<quant> $EVAL --windows 200 --ctx 2048 --device cuda   # verified on CPU with --windows 30 --ctx 256
outputs: JSON {tokens, mean_kld, p99_kld, same_top_pct, ppl_base, ppl_q, ppl_ratio}
steps.resources: Loads base and quant one after the other: VRAM for the larger; RAM holds windows x ctx x vocab x 4 bytes of log-probs (keep windows x ctx <= ~100K tokens for 150K vocabs, or stream). About 1 min per pair on CPU (tiny).
checks: mean_kld and same_top_pct within the policy class

measured (tiny model, 7,650 tokens): W4A16-GPTQ (llm-compressor) 0.00017 / 98.5%; GPTQModel 0.00017 / 98.5%; FP8_DYNAMIC 0.00042 / 97.4%; NF4 0.00062 / 96.9%; NVFP4A16 0.00064 / 97.0%; W4A4 MXFP4 0.0085 / 89.6%
pitfalls: This measures the transformers dequant path; vLLM Marlin kernels give slightly different logits, so re-check through the server (behaviour probes).
GPTQ needs optimum 2.3.0 + gptqmodel in the venv; compressed-tensors and bnb load directly.
steps.verification: Verified on CPU for every HF-format quant made here.

steps.title: Serve the candidate on a scratch port and check it really serves this file at this context
steps.plain: Starts the candidate on a private test port (under the broker lease) and checks the basics a novice would otherwise find out the hard way: it is healthy, lists the model under the planned name, loaded the right file, its chat template supports tools, and every slot really has the planned context.
commands: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:18431/props           # model_path, model_ftype ('Q4_K - Medium'), chat_template_caps, build_info ('b1-8baabd5')
# TabbyAPI (from source, not run): GET /health, GET /v1/models, GET /v1/model (loaded model card), POST /v1/token/encode
outputs: smoke.json: health, models[], props (model_path, model_ftype, chat_template_caps, build_info), slots[].n_ctx, startup log
steps.resources: Model load time (seconds to minutes) plus a few HTTP calls; the VRAM of the planned placement.
checks: /health 200 within the load timeout (ready in 0.55 s for the tiny model)
/v1/models data[].id contains the alias agents will route to
/props model_path == the gated artifact and model_ftype matches the quant
/props chat_template_caps.supports_tools and supports_tool_calls true for agent models (the bundled Qwen2.5 template gives true; a plain one false)
every /slots[].n_ctx >= the target context (verified pitfall: -c 4096 -np 2 on n_ctx_train 1024 gave 1024 per slot and 'capping')
no 'E ' (error) lines in server.log at startup
pitfalls: -c is the TOTAL context shared by the slots: -c 1024 -np 2 gives 512 per slot (verified via /props). Default -np is auto (4 unified slots); set it explicitly.
Default port is 9931 in this build; always pass --port. Without --api-key the server warns 'no API key is set and CORS allows all origins': bind to 127.0.0.1.
TabbyAPI ignores prompt 'echo' ('Not parsed. Only used for OAI compliance'), so likelihood evals cannot run through it.
steps.verification: Verified on CPU with llama-server and tiny models.

steps.title: Template parity and tool-calling probe (agent readiness)
steps.plain: Asks the served candidate questions that need a tool and one that does not, then sends a tool result back. It passes only if the model picks the right tool with valid, schema-correct and sensible arguments, keeps quiet when no tool is needed, and uses the tool's answer. It also proves the served template renders exactly like the original's.
steps.tool: probe_toolcall.py, server_probe.py, probe.py (stdlib); factory models test
commands: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:18431/apply-template -d @$WORK/probe-messages.json   # must byte-match the HF jinja rendering of the same messages and tools (verified: identical)
python3 -I $MFS/probe.py http://127.0.0.1:18931 $WORK/probe-full.json   # feasibility probe: /health, /v1/models, plain chat, /apply-template, tools at temperature 0, tool-result round trip
FACTORY_CONFIG=$WORK/cand-config.json /home/user/software-factory/bin/factory models test <key>   # plain + tool-call probe; exit 1 unless it answers AND calls the probe tool
python3 $LLAMA/scripts/tool_bench.py run --n 10 --temp 0 --temp 1 ...   # llama.cpp's heatmap benchmark (needs uv + pytest/pandas/matplotlib; not run)
inputs: OpenAI-compatible base URL, model id, optional API key
probe cases (must_call with expected name/arguments; no_call)
the HF template rendering of the same messages
outputs: probe.json {cases, passed, pass_rate, results[] with finish_reason, tool_calls, why}
behaviour diff vs the base at temperature 0
steps.resources: About 8 requests per repeat; seconds to a minute at about 100 tok/s.
checks: template parity: /apply-template output byte-identical to the HF jinja rendering

must_call cases: finish_reason == 'tool_calls'; function.name is one of the offered tools and == expected; arguments parse as JSON, validate against the schema, and contain the expected values (a schema-valid but wrong value fails)
no_call case: no tool_calls and no tool markup (<tool_call>, <tool_response>) in content
round trip after role=tool: a text answer that contains the returned value
temperature 0, N repeats; pass_rate >= --min-pass; exit 0 pass / 1 below / 2 server errored on every case
behaviour diff: same greedy probe set on base and candidate; a drop of more than 10 points against the base blocks 'agent' routing
pitfalls: Only the mechanics are verified: a mock server passed 4/4; tiny models failed as they should. In the feasibility run the tool WAS called with the right name and valid JSON but the wrong value ('Europe/London' for Tokyo); with no tools offered it emitted raw <tool_call> markup; after the tool result it emitted <tool_response> text. f16, Q8_0 and Q4_K_M gave byte-identical outputs; IQ4_XS diverged ('America/New_York') despite a KLD of only 0.0012.
With a tools-capable template and tool_choice='required' on a 2,048-token vocab, llama.cpp returned HTTP 400 'Failed to initialize samplers' (grammar init); real vocabularies were not tested.
Tool support depends on the chat template: a quant that lost tokenizer.chat_template fails here even with fine weights.
Mistral templates need 9-character alphanumeric tool-call ids.
steps.verification: Probe mechanics verified (mock pass, tiny-model failures, template parity). No real instruct model was available, so a real pass was never observed.

steps.title: Small task suite with lm-evaluation-harness and llama.cpp scorers
steps.plain: Runs fixed question sets (coding, maths, instruction-following, or the owner's own) against base and candidate under identical settings, so a drop in real ability is caught even when perplexity looks fine.
commands: HF_DATASETS_OFFLINE=1 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 $MF/venvs/lmeval/bin/lm_eval run --model local-chat-completions --model_args model=$NAME-q4km,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:18431/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=4,max_retries=3,tokenizer_backend=None --apply_chat_template --include_path $MF/tasks/mf --tasks mf_gen_local --output_path $WORK/lmeval --log_samples   # verified with a local JSONL task
# local task YAML (verified): dataset_path: json, dataset_kwargs.data_files.test: tasks/mf/gen.jsonl, output_type: generate_until, metric exact_match

$LCPP/llama-perplexity -m $OUT/$NAME-Q4_K_M.gguf -f hellaswag_val_full.txt --hellaswag --hellaswag-tasks 400 -c 512 -ngl 999   # verified on a 4-task file in HellaSwag text format; data via scripts/get-hellaswag.sh
inputs: task names or local task YAMLs (--include_path), mirrored datasets
outputs: $WORK/lmeval/<model>/results_<ts>.json (results.<task>['<metric>,none'], '<metric>_stderr,none', n-samples, task_hashes, lm_eval_version)
samples_*.jsonl with --log_samples
steps.resources: Samples x generation length: e.g. gsm8k 1,319 questions of 200-400 tokens is about 45-90 min single-stream at 100 tok/s, about 3-4x faster with -np 4 and num_concurrent=4 (estimate). Verified local runs took seconds.
checks: exit 0, results JSON exists, n-samples == expected (fail on partial runs)
task_hashes and lm_eval_version identical between base and candidate
candidate_metric >= base_metric - max(abs_tol, 2 x sqrt(se_base^2 + se_cand^2)), abs_tol e.g. 0.02 for accuracy metrics
llama-perplexity --hellaswag: the last row 'N acc_norm% [lo%, hi%]' parses; compare base vs candidate
pitfalls: Likelihood (loglikelihood / multiple_choice) tasks do NOT work against llama-server b11785: lm-eval local-completions failed with KeyError 'token_logprobs' (no echo, new logprobs format). Use llama-perplexity's scorers, lm-eval 'hf'/'vllm' on HF-format quants, or exllamav3 eval/mmlu.py.
tokenizer_backend auto-detect calls /tokenizer_info (vLLM); llama-server returns 404, so pass tokenizer_backend and tokenizer explicitly.
Built-in tasks download datasets from the HF Hub; mirror once and run offline.
Thinking models need a large max_gen_toks and reasoning stripped (llama.cpp --reasoning-format), or exact_match scores 0.
steps.verification: Local generate_until tasks and llama.cpp HellaSwag scoring verified on tiny models; the likelihood failure reproduced.

steps.title: Agentic end-to-end: the Software Factory's own todo job on the candidate
steps.plain: The most realistic test for this owner: route the Software Factory's agents to the candidate and have it complete the same small 'clear completed todos' feature that the factory's scripted end-to-end test uses. It passes only if the job finishes, the tests pass and the tool protocol stays clean.
steps.tool: software-factory bin/factory (run, logs) with a provider config pointing at the candidate
commands: FACTORY_CONFIG=$WORK/cand-config.json /home/user/software-factory/bin/factory run todo-fixture 'Add clearCompleted() to src/todo.js with a test, and a Clear completed button' --delivery branch
inputs: the todo fixture (tests/e2e/harness.py FIXTURE_FILES: src/todo.js, test/todo.test.js, index.html, src/app.js, package.json)
a provider config like examples/strata.json with base_url = the candidate
outputs: exit status (0 merged/delivered, 2 needs-human, 1 failed/rejected/cancelled)
transcript, wall time, tokens, review rounds
steps.resources: Minutes to tens of minutes per run on a local 30B-class model (estimate); one server slot.
checks: 'factory run' exit 0, repeated N=3; record the pass rate
'node --test' passes on the delivered branch and src/todo.js exports clearCompleted
no protocol errors in the transcript (tool results answer the previous turn's calls; reasoning passed back under the key the server sent: the checks tests/e2e/scripted_llm.py enforces)
wall time and tokens recorded; regression gate against the currently deployed model on the same fixture

Uses the GPU for minutes, sequentially with max_concurrency 1 on a one-slot server: schedule it through the broker.

steps.title: Engine throughput sweep: prompt and generation tokens/s at several context depths
steps.plain: Measures how fast the model reads a prompt and writes tokens when 0, 32K or 128K tokens are already in context, for each KV-cache type and split option, on the bare engine, so the numbers are repeatable across quants and upgrades.
steps.tool_version: llama.cpp b11785 (JSON fields: avg_ts, stddev_ts, samples_ts, n_prompt, n_gen, n_depth, type_k, type_v, n_gpu_layers, n_cpu_moe, split_mode, tensor_split, flash_attn, build_commit, gpu_info)
commands: $LCPP/llama-bench -m $OUT/moe.gguf -p 512 -n 128 -d 0,32768 -ncmoe 0,8,12 -ts 24/13 -o json   # llama-bench uses '/' for -ts and ';' for -ot
python3 $LLAMA/scripts/compare-llama-bench.py ...   # compare two builds from an '-o sql' database; not run
outputs: bench.json (one row per model x p/n x depth x ctk x ctv ...)
batched.jsonl (pp, tg, pl, speed_pp, speed_tg)
steps.resources: About r x (one prefill + one decode) per combination; 131K-depth rows dominate (tens of seconds each on 2x3090, estimate). Here 32 rows took under a minute (tiny model).
checks: bench.json parses; every row avg_ts > 0
stddev_ts / avg_ts <= 0.05 on an idle GPU, otherwise re-run (here the CV reached 136-150% on the shared CPU, so the gate is needed)
build_commit in every row == the pinned commit
regression: tg avg_ts at each depth >= 0.9 x the stored baseline for the same model, flags and build

-d depth must fit: the KV holds d + p tokens; check with plan.fit-estimate per depth.
Use -r >= 10 and report the median and CV; a 4M-param model mostly measures overhead.
steps.verification: Verified on CPU (JSON fields, depth sweep, noisy-CV case).

steps.title: Served latency: time to first token and decode tokens/s through the API
steps.plain: Measures what users and agents feel: how long until the first token and how fast the text streams, at several prompt lengths up to the target context, through the real server, with prompt caching defeated.
inputs: depth list up to the deployed context
outputs: bench-server.json: per depth median_ttft_s, median_prompt_tps, median_decode_tps, n_prompt, runs[] with server timings (llama.cpp prompt_per_second / predicted_per_second)

checks: exit 0: every depth streamed tokens (and with --baseline decode_tps >= min-ratio x baseline); 1 regression; 2 errors
n_prompt within 2% of target when the server has /tokenize (llama.cpp), otherwise estimated from chars/token
timings.predicted_n == --gen (ignore_eos honoured; verified 32/32)
TTFT at the largest depth recorded and shown to the user ('at 128K context the first word takes N s')

A unique nonce is prepended and 'cache_prompt': false sent (llama.cpp); TabbyAPI ignores unknown fields, so confirm its prefix cache does not hit.
Not verified against TabbyAPI or Strata; whether TabbyAPI streams usage/timings is unverified.

vram-peak.csv

checks: the breakdown table is present (exit 2 otherwise: the server must run with -lv 4)
per GPU: |actual model - predicted weights| <= max(2 MiB, 5%); same for context vs KV; predicted compute >= actual compute (verified PASS on tiny-mixtral -ncmoe 1 over 2 RPC devices)

steps.title: Scorecard and approver decision
steps.plain: Combines every evaluator's results into one card a novice can read ('Q4_K_M: agrees with the original 96% of the time, fits 128K context on your two GPUs with 13 expert layers in RAM, 62 tokens/s, tool calls 10/10'). The approver agent recommends APPROVE, CHANGES (a new recipe) or ESCALATE; it cannot override a failed number.
commands: # deterministic promotion rule: promote iff artifact.pass && quality.pass && (behaviour.pass || !agent_use) && fit.pass && memory.pass && perf.pass && task_delta_ok
# approver writes decision.md: first line 'DECISION: APPROVE' | 'DECISION: CHANGES' (with the recipe change, e.g. 'IQ4_XS -> Q5_K_M' or 'cache 4,4 -> 8,8') | 'DECISION: ESCALATE'
inputs: artifact gate JSON, quality JSON, probe.json, task results, bench.json, bench-server.json, fit.json, mem.json, hardware.json, plan.json
outputs: scorecard.json + its Grid Card
decision.md
steps.resources: Negligible.
checks: every required evaluator JSON exists, is newer than the artifact and has pass == true
recorded build commit and tool versions equal the pinned ones
scores carry their settings (corpus sha, ctx, chunks, cache type, build), otherwise they are not comparable
CHANGES loops back to the planner at most 2 times, then needs-human
pitfalls: Profiles drift when a server is upgraded (e.g. TabbyAPI dropping EXL2): re-run the smoke and tool probes after every server upgrade (scheduled by the System factory).
steps.verification: Design only.

steps.title: Deterministic gate: hashes, headers, tensor types, licence and quality thresholds
steps.plain: A code-only check (no AI) that the files on disk are exactly the ones the factory made and measured: it re-hashes every file, re-reads the GGUF header with two independent parsers, checks the tensor types still match the quant, the licence is recorded, and the evaluation results are inside the owner's limits. Nothing reaches a server without passing it.
steps.tool_version: prototype; gguf-py 0.19.0 (optional; a stdlib GGUF reader is built in)
outputs: report JSON {ok, failed[], n_checks}; exit 0 pass / 1 fail
steps.resources: Disk-bound hashing (about 15-30 s for a 30 GB variant); the GGUF header parse takes under 1 s even for 100+ GB models.
checks: every files[].sha256 and size match (one flipped byte fails; verified)
GGUF magic and version 2/3 parse with the built-in reader, and gguf-py GGUFReader agrees on tensor count
tensor_count, tensor_types histogram and general.file_type equal the manifest (a Q8_0 renamed as Q4_K_M fails on size, sha, tensor_types {F32:9, Q8_0:30} and file_type 7; verified)
tokenizer.chat_template present
layout path == <name>/<format>/<quant>; no unlisted files
licence.id non-empty; non-allow-listed licences carry a human decision

--require-evals: mean KLD <= max_mean_kld[class], p99 KLD <= max_p99_kld[class], same_top >= min_same_top[class], ppl_ratio <= max_ppl_ratio[class] where enforced, tool_probe.ok == true for agent models
--require-bench: at least one benchmarks[] row with tg_tps
pitfalls: Thresholds are heuristics, not standards: keep them in policy.json per model family.
KLD and PPL must come from the same base logits, text, ctx and chunks.

steps.title: Write the registry entry: models/<name>/<format>/<quant>/manifest.json with provenance and licence
steps.plain: Every model variant lives in its own folder with a manifest: where it came from (base repo and commit, parent variant, imatrix, calibration data), its licence, a size and sha256 for every file, what is inside (architecture, tensor types, context, chat template), the exact command and tool versions, and room for evaluation results, benchmarks and deployments. This one record is what every later step checks, what the GUI shows, and what lets the factory rebuild the quant instead of backing it up.
steps.tool: mf_manifest.py create (stdlib; uses gguf-py when importable)
commands: python3 -I $MFS/mf_manifest.py create $REG/models/$NAME/gguf/Q5_K_M --name $NAME --format gguf --quant Q5_K_M --licence apache-2.0 --base-repo <repo> --base-revision <40-hex sha> --parent $REG/models/$NAME/hf/bf16/manifest.json --imatrix $IM --imatrix-dataset <calib-id> --tool llama-quantize --tool-version 'b11785 (8baabd5)' --command 'llama-quantize --imatrix imatrix.gguf in-bf16.gguf out.gguf Q5_K_M'
$MF/venvs/convert/bin/gguf-dump --json --no-tensors <file.gguf>   # human cross-check of the recorded metadata
inputs: final variant folder with weights + side files (config.json, tokenizer*, chat_template.jinja, LICENSE)
outputs: $REG/models/<name>/<format>/<quant>/manifest.json (status 'candidate', later 'deployable', 'deployed', 'retired', 'pruned' or 'quarantined')
steps.resources: Disk-bound sha256 (about 1-2 GB/s; 15-30 s for 30 GB); RAM small (16 MB buffer).
checks: manifest.json parses; schema == seraphina.model-manifest/1
files[] covers every file in the folder except manifest.json
gguf[] filled for every .gguf (tensor_count, tensor_types, file_type, has_chat_template, chat_template_sha256); split GGUFs list every shard
exl3: hf_config.quantization_config.quant_method == 'exl3' with bits/head_bits/version/calibration
provenance.parent_sha256 == sha256(parent manifest.json); provenance.base_revision is 40-hex
licence.id non-empty and the LICENSE file present (or the licence field in config/README non-empty); gated-licence models flagged before sharing
created_by.command is the exact argv; tool git commit recorded (not the build number)
pitfalls: Make the manifest after the weights are final: gguf-py raises on a truncated GGUF, so create refuses a half-written file.
Evals, benchmarks and deployments are appended data; never edit files[] by hand. The sha list is the contract.
The layout must be exactly models/<name>/<format>/<quant>/ because the gate checks the path against the manifest fields.

GGUF self-records part of its provenance (quantize.imatrix.file/dataset/chunks_count, general.quantization_version) and EXL3 records version/calibration in quantization_config: copy these instead of re-deriving them.
steps.verification: create/verify verified on a test registry (hf/bf16, gguf/Q4_K_M, gguf/Q8_0); the extra provenance fields (calibration, gates, hardware, duration, locks) are design.

provenance.json (schema model-factory/provenance@1)

# server env: OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH, OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE (default f16), OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION, OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL, OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE (default 5m), OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS, OLLAMA_MODELS, OLLAMA_HOST (default 127.0.0.1:11434)

Ollama model <name>:<quant> plus a <name>:previous tag for rollback
steps.resources: `ollama create` copies the GGUF: free disk equal to the file size (it doubles disk use) and about a file copy's time.
checks: 'ollama create' prints 'success'
blob digest in the FROM line == manifest files[].sha256 (verified: sha256-0e1d182e... equals the registry Q4_K_M sha)
/api/show capabilities contains 'tools' for agent models (the GGUF's tool-aware jinja template gave ['tools','completion']; a Go TEMPLATE override without .Tools gave ['completion'])
/api/show details.quantization_level == manifest.quant, details.format == gguf; parameters num_ctx == wanted context

steps.title: Render llama-server settings (single model or router) and lint the flags without loading

Before restarting anything it asks llama-server to parse them with --version, which fails at once on a misspelt, removed or out-of-range flag.
steps.tool_version: llama.cpp b11785 (CPU build here; CUDA not verified); systemd 255
commands:
cat > $REG/deployments/gpu0-llama/serve.flags.env <<'EOF'
LLAMA_ARG_PORT=18081
LLAMA_ARG_CTX_SIZE=262144
LLAMA_ARG_N_PARALLEL=1
LLAMA_ARG_N_GPU_LAYERS=all
LLAMA_ARG_FLASH_ATTN=on
LLAMA_ARG_CACHE_TYPE_K=q8_0
LLAMA_ARG_CACHE_TYPE_V=q8_0
LLAMA_ARG_JINJA=1
LLAMA_ARG_FIT=off
LLAMA_ARG_ENDPOINT_METRICS=1
LLAMA_ARG_API_KEY_FILE=/etc/ai-stack/llama.keys
EOF
(set -a; . $REG/deployments/gpu0-llama/serve.flags.env; set +a; $LCPP/llama-server --version)   # flag lint: exit 1 on a bad flag or value
$LCPP/llama-server -c 262144 -np 1 -ngl all -fa on -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 --jinja -fit off --version   # same lint, argv form

# unit: ExecStart=$LCPP/llama-server -m ${MODEL_FILE} -a ${MODEL_ID} --host 127.0.0.1 with EnvironmentFile=$REG/deployments/%i/serve.env and EnvironmentFile=$REG/deployments/%i/serve.flags.env; Environment=CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 for one-GPU targets

$LCPP/llama-server --models-preset $REG/deployments/router/router.ini --models-max 1 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18082   # router: many registry models behind one port, loaded on demand
# router.ini: version = 1 / [*] c = 262144, jinja = true / [mf/<name>:Q5_K_M] model = $REG/models/<name>/gguf/Q5_K_M/<file>.gguf
inputs: manifest (gguf summary: block_count, expert_count, context_length, split files)
target: GPU(s), port, context per slot, slots
outputs: $REG/deployments/<target>/serve.flags.env
~/.config/systemd/user/mf-llama@.service
optional $REG/deployments/router/router.ini
steps.resources: Lint under 1 s, no GPU. Serving VRAM ≈ GGUF size + KV + 0.5-1.5 GB compute buffers and CUDA context per GPU.
checks: `llama-server <flags> --version` exits 0 (verified: --no-mmap -> 'invalid argument'; bare -fa -> 'expected value'; -ctk q3_k -> 'Unsupported cache type'; LLAMA_ARG_FIT=maybe -> error; good flags -> 0)
systemd-analyze verify exits 0 and prints no 'is not executable' (verified it catches a missing binary)
LLAMA_ARG_PORT set; LLAMA_ARG_HOST unset or 127.0.0.1 (anything else is an audit finding)
LLAMA_ARG_CTX_SIZE == wanted context per slot x LLAMA_ARG_N_PARALLEL
router.ini: every model= path is inside a registry variant that passed gate.registry
pitfalls: -c is the TOTAL context shared by slots: for 262K per agent with --parallel 2 use -c 524288 (unchanged with -kvu; verified via /props).
--fit defaults to on and may silently cut the context (fit-params README: 40960 -> 4096). Set -fit off (or -fitc <ctx>) and assert n_ctx after start.

/health stays unauthenticated with --api-key-file; /v1/models and /props return 401 without the key (verified).

cat > $REG/models/$NAME/exl3/4.0bpw-h6/tabby_config.yml <<'EOF'
model:
  max_seq_len: 262144
  cache_size: 262144
  cache_mode: 8,8
  tensor_parallel: true
  tensor_parallel_backend: nccl

  tool_format: auto
EOF

outputs: config.yml
<model_dir>/<model-name> symlink
<variant>/tabby_config.yml (a registry file, so listed in the manifest)

checks: GET /v1/model/load_config -> has_tabby_config == true and ignored == [] (verified: misspelt 'gpu_spilt' and unknown 'no_mmap' are listed in ignored)
settings.max_seq_len >= the routing entry's context_tokens; cache_size a multiple of 256
cache_mode matches ^([2-8]),([2-8])$ or FP16/Q8/Q6/Q4
tensor_parallel_backend == nccl when NVLink is present (native for PCIe)
quantization_config.quant_method == exl3 (exl2/gptq are rejected by this TabbyAPI)
network.host is 127.0.0.1 or the tailnet address; disable_auth false

--tool-call-parser is a registered parser when --enable-auto-tool-choice is set
after start: /health 200; /v1/models lists --served-model-name; max_model_len >= the routing entry's context_tokens

Unverified: FP8 KV cache speed and support on Ampere; NCCL over NVLink inside vLLM.

steps.title: Switch the target to the new variant atomically, prove it serves, else roll back
steps.plain: The actual deploy, done by the executor as an approved change bundle. It re-runs the gate, saves where 'previous' points, points 'current' at the new variant with an atomic rename, restarts the server, then proves the new model is the one answering: healthy, listed by name, right file, enough context per slot, a plain chat works, the tool-call probe passes and speed is above the floor. If any hard check fails, the previous model is put straight back and checked too, and the failed attempt is kept for diagnosis.
steps.tool: mf_deploy.py deploy + the target's restart command (systemctl)
steps.tool_version: prototype; exercised against llama-server b11785 on CPU with 4.2M-param GGUFs
commands: python3 -I $MFS/mf_deploy.py deploy --deploy-root $REG/deployments --target gpu0-llama --variant $REG/models/$NAME/gguf/Q5_K_M --restart-cmd 'systemctl --user restart mf-llama@gpu0-llama' --base-url http://127.0.0.1:18081/v1 --model-id $NAME-Q5_K_M --api-key-env LLAMA_KEY --tool-probe required --min-ctx 262144 --min-tps 25 --health-timeout 900
journalctl --user -u mf-llama@gpu0-llama --since '-10 min' --no-pager   # captured into the failure record before rollback

curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $LLAMA_KEY" http://127.0.0.1:18081/props | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d["model_path"], d["total_slots"], d["default_generation_settings"]["n_ctx"])'
inputs: target name, restart command, base URL, model id, key env var
outputs: $REG/deployments/<target>/{current, previous} symlinks, serve.env, serve.env.previous, history.jsonl (append-only)
exit 0 deployed / 1 refused by gate / 2 failed and rolled back / 3 rollback failed (needs-human)
steps.resources: Downtime = one restart (model load time) plus probes (under 10 s on GPU). A failed deploy costs two restarts.
checks: gate.registry exits 0 before any switch, else exit 1 and nothing changes
GET /health == 200 within --health-timeout
GET /v1/models data[].id contains --model-id
GET /props model_path is under the new variant (catches an old process answering under the same alias)
/props default_generation_settings.n_ctx >= --min-ctx (per slot, not -c)
plain chat -> 200 with choices[]; tokens/s = timings.predicted_per_second (llama.cpp) or usage.completion_tokens / wall time, >= --min-tps
tool probe (get_time, no args) -> tool_calls[0].function.name == 'get_time' and arguments parse as JSON

on failure: current and previous restored, serve.env restored, restarted, and health + models + model_path pass for the old variant -> exit 2 (verified: tool probe failed -> rolled back to Q8_0; previous still Q4_K_M)
history.jsonl gains one row per attempt and per rollback; concurrent deploys on one target refused by flock (verified)

Write serve.env and symlinks atomically (temp file + rename): a half-written EnvironmentFile makes systemd start the wrong model.
Keep the failed attempt's logs and metrics before restoring, so diagnosis can happen while the old model is already serving (owner decision §31.2).
steps.verification: Full deploy -> failed tool probe -> auto-rollback -> manual Restore cycle verified on CPU.

steps.title: TabbyAPI: hot-swap the loaded model through the admin API and confirm it finished
steps.plain: TabbyAPI can change models without restarting: unload the current one and load the new folder. It streams progress and answers HTTP 200 even when loading fails, so the factory reads the stream and only counts the model as loaded when it sees status 'finished'.
commands: TABBY_ADMIN_KEY=<from the secret store> python3 -I $MFS/mf_tabby_load.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:5000 --admin-key-env TABBY_ADMIN_KEY --model-name $NAME-exl3-4.0bpw --unload-first --timeout 1800
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TABBY_API_KEY" http://127.0.0.1:5000/v1/model   # 503 'No models are currently loaded.' when empty

curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:5000/v1/model/load -H "x-admin-key: $TABBY_ADMIN_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model_name":"<folder>","max_seq_len":262144,"cache_mode":"8,8","tensor_parallel":true}'   # fields from ModelLoadRequest; unverified at runtime

python3 -I $MFS/mf_deploy.py deploy ... --restart-cmd "python3 -I $MFS/mf_tabby_load.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:5000 --admin-key-env TABBY_ADMIN_KEY --model-name <name> --unload-first" --base-url http://127.0.0.1:5000/v1 --model-id <name> --api-key-env TABBY_API_KEY   # same switch/rollback logic
inputs: optional overrides: max_seq_len, cache_mode, cache_size, gpu_split, tensor_parallel
outputs: JSON {ok, last_event, error}; exit 0 loaded / 1 failed
steps.resources: Load time scales with size and disk (tens of seconds for 15-30 GB EXL3 from NVMe); no restart, so the API and its keys stay up.
checks: SSE stream has a data: event with status == 'finished' and model_type == 'model'; any data: {"error":...} event fails (verified: 'The exllamav3 backend is selected, but required dependencies are not installed.' arrived on HTTP 200)
GET /v1/model id == model_name and parameters.max_seq_len >= context_tokens
GET /health status == 'healthy' and issues == []
an unknown model_name -> HTTP 400 before any unload (verified)

--unload-first frees VRAM before loading, so a failed load leaves NOTHING loaded: the rollback must load the previous model_name at once.
If the client disconnects, the load keeps running server-side.
steps.verification: Error path verified; the success path needs CUDA + exllamav3.

ollama cp mf-<name>:q5_k_m mf-<name>:previous   # at every deploy, before re-pointing the live tag

the model profile baseline (tokens_per_s) in the shared facts registry

steps.title: Offer to route agents to the new model (Harness config + Test probes)
steps.plain: A model only helps once agents can use it. The factory adds a provider and a model entry to the Harness config through the same validated save path the GUI uses, runs the factory's own Test probes (a plain reply and a tool call), and only then offers the user 'route agents to it'. Tiers and agents move only after the user accepts and both probes pass.
steps.tool: Software Factory settings.update_config + `factory models test` + `factory doctor --probe`

`factory models` lists the new key with where == local and the right ctx (verified)

steps.title: Prepare and validate the fine-tuning or distillation dataset
steps.plain: Checks the user's training examples before training: the right columns, valid speaker roles, no empty answers, each example ends with the answer to learn, examples fit the length limit, few duplicates, and none of the test questions hidden in the training set.
outputs: dataset report JSON (rows, format, duplicates, eval_rows_also_in_train, tokens_p50/p99/max, frac_over_max_length)
train_pc.jsonl when converted
steps.resources: CPU; linear in rows; seconds for the default 2,000-row sample.
checks: every line parses as JSON with the same column set

format detected: conversational {messages}; prompt_completion {prompt, completion}; preference {prompt, chosen, rejected}; prompt_only {prompt}; text {text}; alpaca {instruction, output}; sharegpt {conversations}
roles in {system, user, assistant, tool, developer}; no empty content without tool_calls; last turn is assistant for SFT

fraction over max_length <= 1%; duplicate-rate warning above 50%
tested: found 9 leaked eval rows and 97% duplicates in a synthetic set; rejected role 'human', a trailing user turn and truncation

steps.title: LoRA/QLoRA fine-tune with Unsloth (GPU)
steps.plain: Teaches a model a new skill by training a small add-on (a LoRA adapter) instead of the whole model, with the base loaded in 4-bit to save GPU memory (QLoRA). The YAML recipe is checked with a dry run first; the adapter can be exported merged, as GGUF or as an adapter.
steps.tool: Unsloth CLI (train, export, eval, doctor, list-checkpoints) or the Python API FastLanguageModel
commands: unsloth doctor --gpus   # exit 1 = a problem; also tests multi-GPU all_reduce
unsloth train -c $MF/recipes/qlora.yaml --dry-run   # VERIFIED: prints the fully resolved config and exits 0 without a GPU
unsloth export $WORK/outputs/<run> $WORK/<name>-merged -f merged-16bit   # formats: merged-16bit, merged-4bit, gguf, lora
unsloth export $WORK/outputs/<run> $WORK/gguf -f gguf -q q4_k_m   # -q: q4_k_m, q5_k_m, q8_0, f16

# Python API (signatures from source): FastLanguageModel.from_pretrained(model_name, max_seq_length=4096, load_in_4bit=True, revision='<sha>', device_map='unsloth_balanced'); FastLanguageModel.get_peft_model(model, r=16, lora_alpha=16, target_modules=[...], use_gradient_checkpointing='unsloth', random_state=3407); model.save_pretrained_merged(dir, tokenizer, save_method='merged_16bit'); model.save_pretrained_gguf(dir, tokenizer, quantization_method=...)
inputs: recipes/qlora.yaml (model; data {dataset | local_dataset, format_type}; training {training_type lora|full, max_seq_length, load_in_4bit, output_dir, num_epochs, learning_rate, batch_size, gradient_accumulation_steps, warmup_steps, max_steps, save_steps, weight_decay, random_seed, packing, train_on_completions, gradient_checkpointing}; lora {lora_r, lora_alpha, lora_dropout, target_modules, use_rslora, use_loftq, use_dora, finetune_*}; logging)
outputs: checkpoints with adapter_config.json + adapter_model.safetensors
exported merged-16bit / gguf / lora folders
sha256 of the dry-run resolved config (provenance)
steps.resources: Unsloth docs minimum VRAM (from search results; the page could not be fetched): QLoRA 7B ~5 GB, 8B ~6 GB, 70B ~41 GB, 405B ~237 GB; LoRA 16-bit 7B ~19 GB, 8B ~22 GB, 70B ~164 GB; more with longer context or batch. On 2x3090: QLoRA up to about 32B on one card; 70B QLoRA only split over both; 16-bit LoRA at 8B or below. Not measured here.
checks: `unsloth train --dry-run` exit 0; sha256 of the printed resolved YAML stored
`unsloth doctor --gpus` exit 0 before the run
training log: no NaN loss; last logged loss < first
adapter gate (ft.trl-peft checks) passes on the checkpoint
the exported merged folder passes download.snapshot-gate and ft.eval-forgetting
pitfalls: CLI defaults: lora_r 64, lora_alpha 16, learning_rate 2e-4, num_epochs 3, max_seq_length 2048, load_in_4bit true, gradient_checkpointing 'unsloth'. Set them explicitly.
Default device_map is 'sequential' (fills GPU0 first); on 2x3090 use 'unsloth_balanced' or 'unsloth'; the planner raises DeviceMapInfeasible rather than spill a bitsandbytes model to CPU.
QLoRA trains against an NF4 copy of the BF16 weights: the owner's EXL2/EXL3/GGUF quants cannot be fine-tuned; keep or re-download the BF16 repo.
The broker must free VRAM held by TabbyAPI/Strata/llama.cpp first.
Licence: unsloth_cli/* and studio/* are AGPL-3.0-only.
steps.verification: Only the CPU dry-run validator ran.

steps.title: LoRA SFT with plain TRL + PEFT (CPU-verified reference path)
steps.plain: The same fine-tune with Hugging Face's own trainer. It was run end to end here on a tiny model on CPU to prove the recipe, data format and gates.
commands: cd $WORK && $MF/venvs/core/bin/trl sft --config $MF/recipes/sft_lora.yaml   # keys: model_name_or_path, model_revision, datasets [{path: json, data_files: <train_pc.jsonl>, split: train}], output_dir, use_peft, lora_r 8, lora_alpha 16, lora_dropout 0, lora_target_modules [q,k,v,o,gate,up,down _proj], max_length, per_device_train_batch_size, learning_rate, max_steps, logging_steps, save_strategy 'no', report_to none, seed 42, data_seed 42 (use_cpu true, dtype float32 for the CPU test)
# QLoRA on GPU (flags in --help; NOT run): --load_in_4bit true --bnb_4bit_quant_type nf4 --use_bnb_nested_quant true --dtype bfloat16 --bf16 true --gradient_checkpointing true
inputs: base folder or Hub id + model_revision sha
outputs: adapter_config.json, adapter_model.safetensors, chat_template.jinja, tokenizer*, README.md, training_args.bin (a pickle: excluded from packages)
trainer log lines with loss
steps.resources: Measured on 4 CPU cores with a 246K-param fixture: 60 steps in 13.6 s; adapter 77.8 KB at F16. A rank-16 all-linear adapter for an 8B Qwen3-class model is about 44M params (about 87 MB BF16), computed not measured.
checks: exit 0; logged loss: last < first (measured 3.695 -> 1.098 over 60 steps)

adapter gate: peft_type LORA; r and target_modules recorded; adapter_model.safetensors (not .bin); every lora_A == [r, in_features] and lora_B == [out_features, r] of the base tensor; #lora_A == #lora_B == layers x target modules (28 = 4 x 7)
adapter_config.base_model_name_or_path equals the pinned base; record the sha in provenance ('revision' is null unless passed)
pitfalls: `trl sft` re-launches itself through `accelerate launch`; multi-GPU DDP was not tested.
data_files paths are resolved against the current directory.
Measured forgetting: general-text perplexity rose from 8.56 to 18.68 after this SFT; always run ft.eval-forgetting.
steps.verification: Run end to end on CPU twice (two skills).

steps.title: Merge a LoRA adapter into its 16-bit base and prove equivalence
steps.plain: Bakes the trained add-on into the model so it becomes one normal model any server can load or the factory can quantise. Checks the merged model gives the same outputs as base plus adapter, and only the layers the adapter touched changed.
steps.tool: merge_adapter.py (PEFT merge_and_unload) + mf_gates.py diff; llama.cpp convert_lora_to_gguf.py
outputs: merged HF folder (safetensors, tokenizer, chat_template.jinja, generation_config.json)
merge report JSON (max_abs_logit_diff_fp32)
optional GGUF LoRA
steps.resources: Under 5 s CPU for the fixture. Real: RAM about 2-4 bytes/param (8B: 16-32 GB; 70B needs GPU or a sharded merge); disk = one more model copy; minutes on CPU for 8B (estimate).
checks: max |logits(base+adapter) - logits(merged)| in fp32 <= 1e-4 on fixed prompts (measured 7.2e-6 and 5.2e-6)
diff gate: changed tensors == adapted modules, all others bit-identical (measured 28 changed / 11 identical: embeddings, norms, lm_head)
merged folder passes download.snapshot-gate; template sha unchanged (download.template-probe)
GGUF LoRA: tensor_count == 2 x adapted modules (measured 56, all F16)
pitfalls: Merge into the 16-bit base, not the 4-bit QLoRA base, or you bake in NF4 rounding (Unsloth merged_16bit does this; merged_4bit is only for further QLoRA).
merge_adapter.py loads the model in fp32 (4 bytes/param); for 8B+ on 64 GB use bfloat16 with device_map='auto' or Unsloth's merged export.
A GGUF LoRA on a heavy quant (Q2-Q3/IQ) is approximate; for production, merge then re-quantise.
steps.verification: Verified on CPU on the fixture.

steps.title: Build gate: task gain versus forgetting, relative to the base
steps.plain: Measures whether the new model got better at the target skill without forgetting general language: compares it with the original on two fixed test sets and passes only if both thresholds hold. Merges and distilled students go through the same gate.
commands: unsloth eval <model> -t mmlu,gsm8k --limit 0.1   # lm-eval wrapper on the GPU box; not run
outputs: ppl-<model>.json: text_tokens, text_ppl, chat_rows, chat_answer_loss, chat_exact_match
steps.resources: Under 20 s per model on CPU (fixture). Real: one forward pass over the eval text; 8B BF16 needs about 17 GB VRAM; 32B+ needs both cards or the GGUF/llama-perplexity route.
checks: forgetting: candidate.text_ppl <= base.text_ppl x 1.10 (warning at 1.05)
task: candidate.chat_answer_loss < base.chat_answer_loss and chat_exact_match >= the user's target
same text_tokens for base and candidate (same tokenizer and file); greedy, seed 0, fp32 reruns identical
merges: per-skill loss <= best parent x 1.15
measured (base / SFT): text_ppl 8.559 / 18.680 (+118%: fails, correctly flagging forgetting); answer_loss 6.458 / 1.250; EM 0.00 / 0.25
pitfalls: Thresholds are proposals tuned on nothing real; calibrate per family on the owner's box.
Perplexity is only comparable with the same tokenizer and text.
Exact match on the training distribution overstates generalisation; keep a held-out set.
steps.verification: Verified on CPU on the fixture.

steps.title: Extract a LoRA from a full fine-tune (ship small)
steps.plain: Turns the difference between a fine-tuned model and its base into a small LoRA add-on, so a fine-tune can be stored and shared in megabytes instead of a full model copy.
outputs: PEFT adapter folder (adapter_config.json, adapter_model.safetensors, README.md)
steps.resources: About 12 s CPU for the fixture. Real: one SVD per linear layer; --cuda for 8B+ (not verified); RAM about two model copies streamed per tensor.
checks: adapter gate passes (measured r=8, lora_alpha=8, 28 A/B pairs)
re-merge round trip: max_abs_diff vs the original fine-tune <= bf16 rounding (measured 0.00195; 28 changed, 11 identical)
ft.eval-forgetting on the re-merged model (extraction is lossy when the real delta has higher rank than --max-rank)
pitfalls: mergekit-extract-lora calls huggingface_hub repo_exists() on every model path while writing its card and crashes (exit 1, ProxyError) when the Hub is unreachable, after the weights are written: run with HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 (verified exit 0).
steps.verification: Verified on CPU on the fixture.

steps.title: Model merges with mergekit (slerp, ties, dare_ties, passthrough, ...)
steps.plain: Combines two or more models of the same family into a new one with no training: blending (slerp), combining what each fine-tune learned (ties/dare) or stacking layers (passthrough). The recipe is a small YAML file and the gates prove the merge did exactly what the recipe says.
commands: $MF/venvs/merge/bin/mergekit-yaml $MF/recipes/m_slerp.yaml $WORK/m-slerp --quiet   # slerp: base_model + 2 models, per-filter t gradients
$MF/venvs/merge/bin/mergekit-yaml $MF/recipes/m_ties.yaml $WORK/m-ties --quiet   # ties: base_model, models with {weight: 1.0, density: 0.5}, normalize: true
$MF/venvs/merge/bin/mergekit-yaml $MF/recipes/m_passthrough.yaml $WORK/m-passthrough --quiet   # slices: layers [0,4) of A + [2,4) of B
inputs: 2+ HF-format models of the same architecture and vocabulary (each passed download.snapshot-gate)
recipe YAML (merge_method, base_model, models | slices, parameters, dtype, tokenizer | tokenizer_source, chat_template)
outputs: merged HF folder with model*.safetensors, config.json, tokenizer, chat_template.jinja, mergekit_config.yml, README.md (regenerated by package.card)
steps.resources: About 10-12 s per merge on CPU (mostly start-up), peak RSS 885 MiB for the fixture. mergekit streams tensors, so RAM stays far below model size; disk = one output copy (70B BF16 about 141 GB). --cuda/--gpu-rich speed up large merges (not verified).
checks: exit 0 and mergekit_config.yml == the recipe (sha256)
identity: slerp with t=0.0 == base_model bit for bit (measured 39/39 identical)
determinism: dare_ties twice with the same --random-seed identical (39/39); a different seed differs (28 changed)
task-vector merges change only tensors where parents differ (ties vs base: 28 changed / 11 identical)
passthrough: num_hidden_layers == sum of slice lengths (6) and tensor count == embed + norm + lm_head + 9 x layers (57)

download.snapshot-gate + template sha + ft.eval-forgetting per skill against each parent (measured text_ppl / capitals_loss / colours_loss: capitals 18.68/1.25/3.82; colours 18.09/5.12/1.27; slerp 13.27/3.56/1.46; ties 16.20/2.89/1.55; dare_ties 34.44/4.09/2.42; passthrough 22.25/1.34/3.50)
pitfalls: Merges need full-precision inputs of the same architecture and vocabulary: the owner's EXL3/GGUF quants cannot be merged.
Task-vector methods (task_arithmetic, ties, dare_*, della, breadcrumbs, sce) need a base_model that is the common ancestor; slerp/nuslerp take exactly 2 models; model_stock needs 3 or more.
Different vocabularies need a tokenizer: {source: base | union | <model>} block (or --unsafe-truncate-embeddings, which skips token-ID checks).
Merge parameters are 'more art than science' (mergekit docs): the per-skill eval decides, not the method name.
Run mergekit with HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 for local work (it calls the Hub while writing cards).
steps.verification: slerp, ties, dare_ties and passthrough verified on CPU with identity, determinism and per-skill checks.

steps.title: Distillation: a smaller student learns from a larger teacher
steps.plain: Makes a smaller, faster model imitate a bigger one: the student is made by keeping some of the teacher family's layers, then trained to match the teacher's token probabilities on the user's prompts. A gate measures how much closer the student got.
steps.tool: mergekit passthrough (student init) + trl distillation (on-policy generalized JSD) + kl_gate.py
commands: $MF/venvs/core/bin/trl distillation --config $MF/recipes/distill.yaml   # keys: model_name_or_path (student), teacher_model_name_or_path, teacher_model_revision, datasets [{path: json, data_files: <prompts.jsonl>}] with a 'prompt' column, beta 0.5 (0 forward KL, 0.5 JSD, 1 reverse KL), temperature 1.0, max_completion_length, learning_rate, max_steps, seed
outputs: student-distilled (HF folder + training_args.bin)
KL reports
steps.resources: 10 steps in 2.4 s on CPU (fixture). Real: teacher and student both resident (a 32B BF16 teacher is about 64 GB, more than 48 GB: use a 4-bit teacher or a teacher server, trl.experimental.server_distillation, not run). Generation dominates the time.
checks: teacher and student vocabularies identical (kl_gate refuses otherwise); teacher vs itself KL == 0.0
mean token KL(teacher || student) after <= 0.9 x before (measured 4.014 -> 3.281, -18%)
top-1 agreement after > before (measured 0.253 -> 0.323)
completions/clipped_ratio < 0.5 at the end (measured 1.0: the tiny student never emitted EOS, which must fail a real run)
student passes download.snapshot-gate (training_args.bin excluded) and ft.eval-forgetting
pitfalls: TRL's DistillationTrainer is on-policy: it generates student completions, needs a 'prompt' column, and generation cost dominates. vLLM integration exists (--use_vllm) but was not tested.
Logit distillation needs the same tokenizer; cross-family distillation needs plain SFT on teacher outputs instead.
Arcee's DistillKit is not on PyPI and was not evaluated.
steps.verification: Verified on CPU on the fixture.

steps.title: (Optional) Publish to the Hugging Face Hub and verify the upload
steps.plain: Uploads a finished model to the user's Hugging Face account, private by default. A gate first makes sure nothing unsafe or private goes up (no pickles, tokens or local paths; every file matches its provenance); after upload the online copy is tagged and checked byte for byte.
steps.tool: mf_gates.py publish + hf repos/upload/tag + hf cache verify

hf upload <user>/<name> $WORK/pub/<name> . --exclude 'training_args.bin' --exclude '*.pt' --exclude '.cache/*' --commit-message '<name> v1 (recipe sha256 ...)'   # resumable, multi-commit
hf repos tag create <user>/<name> v1 --revision <sha> -m 'Model Factory build v1'
inputs: folder that passed the gates and package.card
write token from the secret store (never in files)
outputs: Hub repo at commit <sha> with tag v1
verification report
steps.resources: Upload-bandwidth bound (the model size once; xet dedups unchanged chunks on re-upload, a design claim not tested). CPU only.
checks: publish gate (verified): no pickle files; no hf_ token pattern in text files; no /home/, /root/, /tmp/ or C:\Users\ paths in README/configs; provenance.json present and every outputs_sha256 matches; no files outside provenance (a file edited after carding fails 'sha256 differs from provenance')

`hf upload` has no --dry-run: the publish gate is the dry run.
